## Learning Objectives

1. Know when to use analysis of variance
2. Understand that the null hypothesis for analysis of variance is no difference in means across groups or values of explanatory variables
3. Understand how to decompose variance into its sources
4. Understand the problem of multiple hypothesis testing

# To the board...

```{r anova-board-helpers}
#| include: false

# ---- shared look ------------------------------------------------------------

line_col <- "steelblue"
pt_col <- "tomato"

theme_slides <- function() {
    theme_cowplot() +
        theme(
            axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 22),
            strip.text = element_text(size = 20),
            plot.title = element_text(size = 22, hjust = 0.5)
        )
}

ylab_i <- expression(italic(Y))

# write a small number as TeX scientific notation, e.g. 1.2 \times 10^{-5}
sci_tex <- function(x, digits = 2) {
    if (x >= 0.001) {
        return(as.character(signif(x, digits)))
    }
    expo <- floor(log10(x))
    mant <- signif(x / 10 ^ expo, digits)
    paste0("$", mant, " \\times 10^{", expo, "}$")
}

# ---- two small examples: three groups, five observations each ---------------

# the same within-group deviations, shuffled differently in each group
make_groups <- function(means, w) {
    data.frame(group = rep(LETTERS[1:3], each = 5),
               y = rep(means, each = 5) +
                   c(w, w[c(3, 1, 5, 2, 4)], w[c(2, 4, 1, 5, 3)]))
}

# group means far apart compared to the spread within groups
small_data <- make_groups(c(1.2, 2.4, 3.6), c(-0.5, 0.3, 0.6, -0.4, 0))

# group means close together compared to the spread within groups
overlap_data <- make_groups(c(3.2, 3.6, 4.0), c(-1.3, 0.8, 0.3, 1.4, -1.2))

anova_parts <- function(d) {
    y_bar <- mean(d$y)
    group_mean <- ave(d$y, d$group)
    n_groups <- nlevels(factor(d$group))
    ss_group <- sum((group_mean - y_bar) ^ 2)
    ss_error <- sum((d$y - group_mean) ^ 2)
    df_group <- n_groups - 1
    df_error <- nrow(d) - n_groups
    f <- (ss_group / df_group) / (ss_error / df_error)
    list(ss_y = sum((d$y - y_bar) ^ 2),
         ss_group = ss_group,
         ss_error = ss_error,
         df_group = df_group,
         df_error = df_error,
         f = f,
         p = pf(f, df_group, df_error, lower.tail = FALSE))
}

small_parts <- anova_parts(small_data)
overlap_parts <- anova_parts(overlap_data)

# type: "raw" (data and overall mean), "total" (Y to the overall mean),
#       "group" (group means to the overall mean), "error" (Y to its group mean),
#       "means" (data, group means and overall mean)
groups_plot <- function(d, type = "raw", title = NULL, f_label = NULL,
                        small = FALSE) {
    txt <- ifelse(small, 5, 7)
    d$x_pos <- as.numeric(factor(d$group)) + rep(c(-0.24, -0.12, 0, 0.12, 0.24), 3)
    d$g_mean <- ave(d$y, d$group)
    y_bar <- mean(d$y)
    g <- data.frame(x = 1:3, g_mean = tapply(d$y, d$group, mean))

    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x_pos, y)) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = y_bar, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40")
    if (type == "total") {
        p <- p + geom_segment(aes(xend = x_pos, yend = y_bar), color = "black",
                              linewidth = 1.2)
    }
    if (type == "group") {
        p <- p + geom_segment(aes(y = g_mean, xend = x_pos, yend = y_bar),
                              color = line_col, linewidth = 1.2)
    }
    if (type == "error") {
        p <- p + geom_segment(aes(xend = x_pos, yend = g_mean), color = "firebrick",
                              linewidth = 1.2)
    }
    if (type %in% c("group", "error", "means")) {
        p <- p + geom_segment(data = g, aes(x = x - 0.34, xend = x + 0.34,
                                            y = g_mean, yend = g_mean),
                              inherit.aes = FALSE, color = line_col, linewidth = 2.5)
        p <- p + annotate("text", x = 3.4, y = g$g_mean[3], label = "hat(Y)[j]",
                          parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, size = txt, color = line_col)
    }
    p <- p +
        geom_point(color = pt_col, size = ifelse(small, 3, 4),
                   alpha = ifelse(type == "group", 0.35, 1)) +
        annotate("text", x = 3.95, y = y_bar - 0.3, label = "bar(Y)", parse = TRUE,
                 hjust = 1, size = txt)
    if (!is.null(f_label)) {
        p <- p + annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 5.3, label = f_label, parse = TRUE,
                          hjust = 0, size = 7)
    }
    if (!is.null(title)) {
        p <- p + ggtitle(title)
    }
    p <- p +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = LETTERS[1:3]) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.4, 3.95), ylim = c(0, 5.6)) +
        xlab("Group") +
        ylab(ylab_i) +
        theme_slides()
    if (small) {
        p <- p + theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
                       axis.title = element_text(size = 14))
    }
    p
}

# ---- the F distribution under H0 --------------------------------------------

anova_f_plot <- function(f_obs, df1, df2, xmax, label_left = TRUE) {
    d <- data.frame(x = seq(0.02, xmax, length.out = 600))
    d$y <- df(d$x, df1, df2)
    tail_d <- d[d$x >= f_obs, ]
    x_t <- f_obs + 0.2 * (xmax - f_obs)
    y_t <- max(0.5 * df(x_t, df1, df2), 0.02)
    ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
        geom_area(data = tail_d, fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.7) +
        geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = f_obs, color = line_col, linewidth = 1.3) +
        annotate("text", x = f_obs + ifelse(label_left, -1, 1) * 0.02 * xmax, y = 0.9,
                 label = "observed F", hjust = ifelse(label_left, 1, 0), size = 7,
                 color = line_col) +
        annotate("text", x = f_obs + 0.35 * (xmax - f_obs), y = 0.4, label = "P-value",
                 size = 7, color = "firebrick") +
        annotate("segment", x = f_obs + 0.35 * (xmax - f_obs), xend = x_t, y = 0.34,
                 yend = y_t, color = "firebrick",
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.12, "in"))) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, xmax), ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
        xlab(expression(F == MS[group] / MS[error])) +
        ylab("Density") +
        theme_slides()
}
```

## [Analysis of variance]{.alert}: do the group means differ?

::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}
::: {.column width="45%"}
Is the mean of $Y$ the same in every group?

A small example: three groups, five observations each

::: {.fragment}
ANOVA splits the variation in $Y$ into two sources: variation [among]{.alert} the group means and variation [within]{.alert} the groups
:::
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "5in"

groups_plot(small_data, "raw")
```
:::
:::

## Sum of squares: $SS_Y$ {.top-align}

::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}
$$
SS_Y = \sum (Y_i - \overline{Y})^2
$$

The total variation in $Y$: how far every observation is from the overall mean, $\overline{Y}$
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "5in"

groups_plot(small_data, "total")
```
:::
:::

## Sum of squares: $SS_{group}$ {.top-align}

::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}
$$
SS_{group} = \sum n_j (\hat{Y}_j - \overline{Y})^2
$$

::: {.incremental}
- $\hat{Y}_j$ is the mean of group $j$: the prediction for every observation in that group
- $n_j$ is the number of observations in group $j$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$SS_{group}$ is [big]{.alert} when the group means are far from $\overline{Y}$
:::
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "5in"

groups_plot(small_data, "group")
```
:::
:::

## Sum of squares: $SS_{error}$ {.top-align}

::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}
$$
SS_{error} = \sum (Y_i - \hat{Y}_j)^2
$$

Compare each data point to the mean of its [own group]{.alert}

::: {.fragment}
The variation within groups: what the groups do not explain
:::
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "5in"

groups_plot(small_data, "error")
```
:::
:::

## Sum of squares: all together

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.fragment}
$SS_Y$ $=$

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 3.3
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "3.2in"

groups_plot(small_data, "total", small = TRUE)
```

$\sum (Y_i - \overline{Y})^2$
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.fragment}
$SS_{group}$ $+$

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 3.3
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "3.2in"

groups_plot(small_data, "group", small = TRUE)
```

$\sum n_j (\hat{Y}_j - \overline{Y})^2$
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.fragment}
$SS_{error}$

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 3.3
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "3.2in"

groups_plot(small_data, "error", small = TRUE)
```

$\sum (Y_i - \hat{Y}_j)^2$
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Mean squares

A sum of squares gets bigger with every data point we add, so we divide by the degrees of freedom to get a [mean square]{.alert}

$$
MS_{group} = \frac{SS_{group}}{df_{group}} \qquad\qquad MS_{error} = \frac{SS_{error}}{df_{error}}
$$

::: {.incremental}
- $df_{group} = (\text{number of groups}) - 1$
- $df_{error} = N - (\text{number of groups})$: we estimate one mean for each group
:::

::: {.fragment}
In our example, 3 groups and $N =$ 15: $df_{group} =$ `r small_parts$df_group` and $df_{error} =$ `r small_parts$df_error`
:::

## Sum of squares and mean squares in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true

y_bar <- mean(small_data$y)
group_mean <- ave(small_data$y, small_data$group)

ss_y <- sum((small_data$y - y_bar) ^ 2)
ss_group <- sum((group_mean - y_bar) ^ 2)
ss_error <- sum((small_data$y - group_mean) ^ 2)

ss_y
ss_group + ss_error

ms_group <- ss_group / (3 - 1)
ms_error <- ss_error / (15 - 3)

ms_group
ms_error
```

## Comparing $MS_{group}$ to $MS_{error}$

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| out-width: "10in"

plot_grid(groups_plot(small_data, "means", title = expression(MS[group] > MS[error])),
          groups_plot(overlap_data, "means", title = expression(MS[group] < MS[error])),
          nrow = 1)
```

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
The group means are far apart compared to the spread within each group
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
The group means are close together compared to the spread within each group
:::
:::
:::

## $F$-statistic {.top-align}

$$
F = \frac{MS_{group}}{MS_{error}}
$$

::: {style="margin-top: -0.6em;"}
How much more variation between groups ($MS_{group}$) compared to variation in "residuals" ($MS_{error}$), bounded $[0, \infty)$
:::

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| out-width: "8.8in"

f_small <- paste0('F == "', sprintf("%.2f", small_parts$f), '" ~ "(big)"')
f_overlap <- paste0('F == "', sprintf("%.2f", overlap_parts$f), '" ~ "(small)"')

plot_grid(groups_plot(small_data, "means", title = expression(MS[group] > MS[error]),
                      f_label = f_small),
          groups_plot(overlap_data, "means", title = expression(MS[group] < MS[error]),
                      f_label = f_overlap),
          nrow = 1)
```

## The null hypothesis

::: {.incremental}
- $H_0$: $\mu_A = \mu_B = \mu_C$, all of the group means are equal
- $H_A$: not all of the means are equal
:::

::: {.fragment}
For any number of groups, $k$: $H_0$: $\mu_1 = \mu_2 = \dots = \mu_k$
:::

::: {.fragment}
If $H_0$ is true, $MS_{group}$ and $MS_{error}$ both estimate the variation within groups, so $F \approx 1$
:::

::: {.fragment}
If some means differ, $MS_{group}$ gets bigger than $MS_{error}$ and $F$ gets big
:::

## Null hypothesis test with $F$

If $H_0$ is true, $F$ follows an [F-distribution]{.alert} with $df_{group}$ and $df_{error}$ degrees of freedom

::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "4.6in"

anova_f_plot(overlap_parts$f, overlap_parts$df_group, overlap_parts$df_error,
             xmax = 6, label_left = FALSE)
```

$F_{`r overlap_parts$df_group`,`r overlap_parts$df_error`} =$ `r round(overlap_parts$f, 2)`, $P =$ `r round(overlap_parts$p, 2)`

$df_{group} =$ `r overlap_parts$df_group`, $df_{error} =$ `r overlap_parts$df_error`
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "4.6in"

anova_f_plot(small_parts$f, small_parts$df_group, small_parts$df_error,
             xmax = 40)
```

$F_{`r small_parts$df_group`,`r small_parts$df_error`} =$ `r round(small_parts$f, 1)`, $P =$ `r sci_tex(small_parts$p)`

$df_{group} =$ `r small_parts$df_group`, $df_{error} =$ `r small_parts$df_error`
:::
:::
:::

## Null hypothesis test with $F$

The [P-value]{.alert} is the probability of an $F$ at least as big as the observed $F$, if $H_0$ is true

::: {.fragment}
If $P \leq 0.05$: reject $H_0$

If $P > 0.05$: fail to reject $H_0$
:::

::: {.fragment}
If we reject $H_0$: at least one group mean is different from the others
:::

## Finding $F$ and the P-value in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true

f_stat <- ms_group / ms_error
f_stat

pf(q = f_stat, df1 = 3 - 1, df2 = 15 - 3, lower.tail = FALSE)
```

::: {.fragment}
`q` is our $F$ statistic, `df1` is $df_{group}$, `df2` is $df_{error}$

$P < 0.05$, so we reject $H_0$: at least one group mean is different from the others
:::

## Example ANOVA for multiple groups in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true

# make some pretend data
groups <- rep(LETTERS[1:3], each = 10)
y <- 1.2 * as.numeric(as.factor(groups)) + rnorm(30, mean = 0, sd = 0.5)

dat_groups <- data.frame(group = groups, y = y)

head(dat_groups, n = 3)
```

## Example ANOVA for multiple groups in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "5in"

ggplot(dat_groups, aes(x = group, y = y)) + geom_boxplot()
```

## Example ANOVA for multiple groups in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "5in"

ggplot(dat_groups, aes(x = group, y = y)) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = group)) +
    scale_color_discrete(palette = c("tomato", "purple4", "dodgerblue3"))
```

## Example ANOVA for multiple groups in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true

mod_group <- lm(y ~ group, data = dat_groups)
anova(mod_group)
```

## Assumptions of ANOVA for groups

- Random and independent samples
- Normal distribution for each group
- Equal variances within each group

## What to do if assumptions are not met?

- Do ANOVA anyway (if deviations are minor)
- Transform
- More advanced stats

## Interpreting ANOVA for groups

ANOVA does not tell you which group(s) is/are different!  Just that a difference exists

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 3
#| out-width: "5in"

ggplot(dat_groups, aes(x = group, y = y)) + geom_boxplot()
```

## Interpreting ANOVA for groups

If we want to know which groups are different, we need to do a "post hoc" test

- Post hoc tests are designed to account for multiple comparisons
- What are multiple comparisons and why can't we just do multiple $t$-tests?

## Pos hoc tests and multiple comparisons

Which groups are different?  Just do $t$-tests between all pairwise comparisons, right?

- The problem: doing multiple $t$-tests leads to a false positive rate $> \alpha$
- If we do 3 pairwise comparisons with $t$-tests and $\alpha = 0.05$ for each one, then probability of at least 1 false positive is:

```{r}
#| echo: true

prob_false_positive <- 1 - dbinom(0, size = 3, prob = 0.05)
prob_false_positive
```

## Pos hoc tests and multiple comparisons

```{r}
#| echo: true

prob_false_positive <- 1 - dbinom(0, size = 3, prob = 0.05)
prob_false_positive
```

Each $t$-test is like a coin toss with "heads = false positive", the more you do, the more likely you'll get at least one "heads = false positive"

## Pos hoc tests and multiple comparisons

So we use a post hoc test:

```{r}
#| echo: false

# annoying, but we have to pass the model through the `aov` function
aov_group <- aov(mod_group)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# annoying, but we have to pass the model through the `aov` function
aov_group <- aov(mod_group)

# "Tukey Honest Significant Difference"
TukeyHSD(aov_group)
```

## Pos hoc tests and multiple comparisons

So we use a post hoc test:

```{r}
#| echo: true

# "Tukey Honest Significant Difference"
TukeyHSD(aov_group)
```

## Pos hoc tests and multiple comparisons

The adjusted Confidence Intervals and $P$-values make sure that the overall $\alpha$ remains at the desired level, usually 0.05

# Multi-factor ANOVA

## Learning Objectives

1. What is a multi-factor ANOVA, when do you use it, and how?

# To the board...

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true

# make some pretend data
restoration <- factor(rep(c("restored", "control"), each = 30))
impact <- factor(rep(c("low", "high"), 30),
                 levels = c("low", "high"))

# compute expected response
fish_biomass <- -1 * as.numeric(impact) + 3 * as.numeric(restoration) -
  1 * as.numeric(impact) * as.numeric(restoration)

# add some noise
set.seed(123)
fish_biomass <- fish_biomass + rnorm(60, mean = 0, sd = 1)

dat <- data.frame(restoration, impact, fish_biomass)
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R*

```{r}
# have a look at pretend data
head(dat)
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

ggplot(dat, aes(x = restoration, y = fish_biomass,
                fill = impact)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "YlGnBu", direction = -1)
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 2
#| out-width: "5in"

gp <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = restoration, y = fish_biomass,
                fill = impact)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "YlGnBu", direction = -1)
gp
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R*

```{r}
#| echo: true

mod <- lm(fish_biomass ~ impact + restoration, data = dat)
anova(mod)
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R*

How do we see the estimate of the effects?

```{r}
#| echo: true

summary(mod)
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R*

But looking at the graph, it also seems like the effect of restoration depends on human impact

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 2
#| out-width: "5in"

gp
```

The two effects [interact]{.alert}

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R* **with interactions**

The asterisk `*` between terms allows for interactions

```{r}
#| echo: true

mod_interactions <- lm(fish_biomass ~ impact * restoration,
                       data = dat)
anova(mod_interactions)
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R* **with interactions**

And the interaction effect is meaningful!

```{r}
#| echo: true

summary(mod_interactions)
```

Higher human impact *reduced* the effect of restoration

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R* **with interactions**

If you want to do a post-hock test, how would you do it?

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R* **with interactions**

If you want to do a post-hock test, how would you do it? *Just like before!*

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

aov_interactions <- aov(mod_interactions)
TukeyHSD(aov_interactions)
```

```{r}
aov_interactions <- aov(mod_interactions)
TukeyHSD(aov_interactions)
```

## Example multi-factor ANOVA in *R* **with interactions**

```{r}
foo <- TukeyHSD(aov_interactions)
foo[3]
```
